title: Council committee appointments and economic strategy session
subtitle: Make It Kitchener refresh, data and digital strategies, Laurier board change and a closed session on three matters.
overview: A special Council meeting began with approval to hold a closed session on a land acquisition, potential litigation, and a negotiations and solicitor-client privilege matter {{vote:m1}}. The minutes report no public outcome from that session.

Most of the afternoon was a strategic session, which had no web stream. Council heard about the CityWide Data Strategy and Digital Kitchener, including where technology and artificial intelligence could improve service. Council also reviewed the midpoint of Make It Kitchener 2.0, the ten-year economic development strategy. Staff cited pressures such as trade and tariff uncertainty, high interest rates, slower home sales, downtown office vacancies and changes to international student programs. Council ranked its priority focus areas for the refresh. Neither session item produced a formal decision.

In the evening Council filled its 2025-2026 committee appointments. Most existing appointments carried over. The Community and Infrastructure Services chair is Councillor Schnider and the vice-chair is Councillor Johnston. Councillor Singh now represents Council on the Wilfrid Laurier University Board of Governors. The minutes record these appointments as voted on and carried, without separate motion numbers.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed session after the special meeting to discuss a land acquisition, potential litigation, and a negotiations and solicitor-client privilege matter {{vote:m1}}.

debate: The chair noted that one councillor could not attend but asked that their existing committee appointments be maintained, and Council proceeded on that basis.
Two councillors were nominated for chair of the Community and Infrastructure Services Committee. One declined to stand in order to seek the vice-chair role, and the other was acclaimed as chair.
For the Wilfrid Laurier University Board of Governors, two members separately offered to nominate the same councillor, who accepted.

A councillor asked whether the Centre in the Square board appointment runs for the full four-year term. The Clerk said staff would take that away and advise Council if no change was needed, and the three current members were reappointed for now.
